A sixth candidate, a Rhysida ransomware leak of Berlin state government data, was dropped for being dated 2026-09-04, two days stale relative to today and outside the yesterday/today announcement window. Net: zero new security entries this run, a genuinely quiet day once duplicates were removed. The AI lane's proposed 'xAI Grok 4.7 launches ~Sept 12' and the bigtech lane's 'Samsung Galaxy Unpacked S27' were both dropped for resting only on low-credibility aggregator sites interpreting a tweet/rumor, not an organisation's own statement -- below the sourcing bar even at 'rumored'. Also dropped: an AWS 'South America (Chile) region' candidate whose only Chile-specific source didn't state a date more precise than the year, and whose second cited source was actually about the (separately, already-filed) Saudi Arabia region -- a mismatched citation not worth filing on.
concerns: Recurring near-duplicate-title workaround still needed (flagged in the 2026-09-02, 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-05 run logs): filing 'Azure AI Foundry retires GPT-5' alongside the already-filed GPT-4.1 and GPT-4o Foundry retirements, and 'Amazon Bedrock retires Nova Canvas and Nova Reel' alongside the already-filed Nova Sonic/Nova Premier retirement, both required maximally distinct, fully-spelled-out titles to stay clear of src/lib/id.ts's sameTitle() 0.6 threshold.
